draft.title: Protecting ancient sites
card: Ancient sites can be damaged or lost. Threats include building work, war, looting and tourism.
Looting is stealing objects from a site. It destroys the context of a find, so we lose information about where and how it was used.
UNESCO is a United Nations agency. It keeps a list of World Heritage sites that are important to all people, and it helps countries protect them.
In the 1960s, Egypt built the Aswan High Dam, and its lake would have flooded the temples of Abu Simbel. The temples were cut into blocks and rebuilt on higher ground.
draft.remember: Sites face many threats, and people act to protect them, as they did at Abu Simbel.

a.q: Why was the Abu Simbel temple complex moved in the 1960s?
opts: A dam's rising lake would have flooded it
A war was about to destroy it
Looters had stolen most of its stone
Too many tourists were damaging it
a.why: The Aswan High Dam created a lake that would have covered the temples, so they were cut into blocks and rebuilt on higher ground. Tourism is a real threat to sites, but it was not the reason for this move.
a.clue: Think about what the new dam would have done to the land by the river.

b.q: Thieves dig into an ancient tomb at night and carry off statues to sell. Which threat is this?
opts: Looting
Building
War
Tourism
b.why: Stealing objects from a site is looting. It also destroys the context of the finds, so we lose information about the past. Tourism is different because visitors usually do not steal objects.
b.clue: Look at what the thieves do with the statues.

a.best: A dam's rising lake would have flooded it

problems.detail: The clue names the dam directly ('what the new dam would have done'), which points straight to the only option that mentions a dam. A student can answer without knowing the idea.

'Context' here means where a find lay and what was around it. In point 2, the same word means 'what was happening at the time'. Using one word with two meanings in the same chapter, without saying so, may confuse Year 7 students.

proposal.title: Protecting ancient sites
card: Ancient sites can be damaged or lost. Threats include building work, war, looting and tourism, as large crowds of visitors can wear sites down.
Looting is stealing objects from a site. Once an object is taken, we no longer know exactly where it lay or what was found with it, so we lose information about how it was used.
UNESCO is a United Nations agency. It keeps a list of World Heritage sites that are important to all people, and it helps countries protect them.
In the 1960s, Egypt built the Aswan High Dam, and its lake would have flooded the temples of Abu Simbel. The temples were cut into blocks and rebuilt on higher ground.
